title: feat(browser-use): support concurrent sessions sharing a Chrome profile
before: At parent commit 91a868d9c183e46771993aff89c7f7bbfd509b25, the checkout contains no packages/browser-use tree and no pinned Browser Use SDK, Chrome bridge, Playwright session, or related tests. The requested concurrent-session capability therefore has no implementation state in this parent under the scoped package.
after: At pinned commit 1c193a9a3e3e09db6cd44ab60b4515f2220a6175, a new Playwright-based Browser Use SDK and local Chrome bridge exist. The implemented contract is explicitly single-session per OS user: one session may control multiple tabs, a second session fails with BROWSER_USE_BUSY, and future concurrent sessions are documented as follow-up work requiring isolated ownership, event routing, cleanup, and reconnect behavior. Thus the pinned after-state does not establish support for concurrent Browser Use sessions sharing one Chrome profile.
diff: The pinned commit adds the Browser Use package, bilingual architecture documentation, a framed local Chrome-extension transport with per-user socket ownership and stale-socket recovery, Playwright CDP target/session routing, per-tab attachment serialization, runtime start/stop and stale-session invalidation, SDK proxies, and extensive unit tests. These changes coordinate one Browser Use runtime across multiple tabs and overlapping attach/cleanup operations, and reject a second runtime that attempts to bind the live bridge socket. They do not implement the target issue's multi-session isolation contract; the design explicitly places concurrent-session ownership/event-routing/cleanup/reconnect isolation in future work. Because the issue body, discussion, timeline, and linked PR are unavailable and the pinned commit identifies a different feature (#11241), this is retained as a non-promotable bounded episode with no target Change Actions or Issue Workflow.

    form classifies now; other channels keep the unwrapped form.

    reports its CDP events (a microtask in CRSession plus the in-process
    dispatcher's setImmediate), so an open+close pair delivered in one chunk
    left a phantom dialog that blocked the tab. Each tab now traces dialog
    openings and closes in bridge order and drops a delivered dialog the
    bridge already reported closed; a close with no traced opening (a dialog
    open before the tab was attached) is never charged to a later dialog, and

    disagrees with the requested CSS region, deriving the real ratio from
    Chrome's own pixels (measured / (width * scale)).

    ancestor sweep rejects symlinks, and macOS reaches os.tmpdir() through
    /var -> /private/var, so the tests failed locally on macOS.

    The esbuild banner declared require/__filename/__dirname/process bindings
    the bundle never uses, so any bundled module declaring one of them built
    green but failed to load; drop it (and the unused .wasm loader) and import
    dist/index.js after bundling so an unloadable bundle fails the build.
    
    When start() fails after listen (chmod, handshake), a peer validated in
    between kept server.close() waiting forever; destroy and clear the
    accepted sockets first, mirroring stop(). net.Server has no
    closeAllConnections(), so that is the whole fix.
    
    Tests now cover the QWEN_BROWSER_USE_SOCKET_PATH override, a hello with a
    mismatched protocol version or extension id, onConnectionChange on the
    real transport, an in-flight request when the extension disconnects and
    the configured request budget, the ok:false error-code mapping,
    FrameDecoder split-frame reassembly and its length ceiling, the
    start-failure teardown, and all five schema refine predicates.
    
    * fix(browser-use): mirror the contract bounds in the SDK and state the documented limits
    
    nth() now rejects indexes outside the contract's -10000..10000 before
    dispatch, and all() fails closed when the plan already has 32 steps or
    the match count exceeds what nth() can address, instead of handing back
    locators that only fail on first use. Both evaluate script builders
    normalise method-shorthand and class-method sources the way Playwright
    does (compile-only vm.Script probe, then a function prefix), so those
    well-typed callbacks no longer die as a page-side SyntaxError.
    
    providerTab clamps title and url to the claimTab schema's 20000-char cap
    so the documented openTabs() -> claimTab() round trip survives long URLs,
    and orderOpenTabs() establishes the http(s)-only, newest-first listing
    the model documentation promises. downloadMedia derives the file name
    from the URL path only for http(s) sources and leaves blob:/data: names
    to the browser.
    
    The model-facing documentation now states the 1s read default, that
    dom_cua.scroll's x/y are wheel deltas rather than coordinates, and that
    a cross-origin resource without CORS headers cannot be downloaded from
    the page origin; the design docs record that boundary as follow-up work.
    Tests pin every one of these, plus buildLocator's frame, combinator,
    filter and positional branches, the file-chooser SDK surface, and the
    claimTab argument guards.
    
    * fix(browser-use): keep background tab registration from moving the selection
    
    registerTab selected every tab it registered, and two of its callers are
    background paths (derivedTabTracked, syncDerivedTabs via tabs.list), so
    a read-only tabs.list could move tabs.selected onto a popup. Selection is
    now set only by newTab and claimTab from the info they return.
    
    Also: tabs.get is allowed while a dialog is open, matching tabs.list and
    tabs.selected, which already return the dialog-safe TabInfo; the
    auxiliary-button click moves Playwright's tracked cursor before sending
    the CDP button events so a later wheel lands where the click did; the
    dead providerTabId lookup is removed; openTabs applies orderOpenTabs.
    
    Tests: the runtime test file mocks node:timers so vi.useFakeTimers()
    actually controls the input drain bound (the 250ms test drops to ~0ms),
    and new cases pin the drain clearTimeout, the registration probe's
    session detach, promptText pass-through, tabs.get under a dialog, the
    openTabs/claimTab fail-closed guards and ordering, popup adoption from
    derivedTabTracked, the abandoned navigation waiter's swallowed rejection,
    the uploadFiles path guards, and the screencast fallback and byte budget
    on the unconstrained capture path.
    
    * test(browser-use): pin the element bindings the runtime gives evaluate scripts
    
    The SDK emits scripts that read the free variables `element` and
    `elements`, and the runtime binds them when it compiles the script inside
    the page; no test ran either page-side callback, so swapping the binding
    name on one side kept the suite green while every locator.evaluate would
    throw a ReferenceError in production. Run the real callbacks with fake
    elements so the contract is pinned from both ends.
    
    * fix(browser-use): fail closed on page-controlled strict-mode text and prefer contained media over anchor hrefs
    
    * fix(browser-use): bound page title reads and download a located anchor's file over its icon
    
    * fix(browser-use): correct media downloads and frame composition
    
    * fix(browser-use): bound locator.count and allTextContents by the caller deadline
    
    * fix(browser-use): preserve native snapshots for DOM CUA
    
    Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
    
    * fix(browser-use): classify a closed tab from the tab's own state
    
    The pinned playwright-core client renders a closed target as a plain Error:
    only TimeoutError sets `name`, so the `name === 'TargetClosedError'` branch
    in sanitizeOperationError never fired, and because evaluate-channel text
    fails closed by design, a tab that closed or crashed while a page command
    ran was reported as OPERATION_FAILED instead of the documented STALE_TAB.
    
    Decide tab-gone in the dispatcher from `tab.stale` and `page.isClosed()`,
    which the page observers keep current, before the text classifier runs.
    Drop the dead name branch and replace the test that fabricated the name
    with one built the way the client builds the error, plus dispatch-level
    cases for both signals that fail without the dispatcher check.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * fix(browser-use): close six fail-open paths in the playwright adapter
    
    Round-22 review found six Critical defects in the new package; each is
    fixed at its root and pinned by a test that goes red without the fix:
    
    - locator.evaluateAll opened a second full timeout window after the
      attach wait had consumed the caller's budget; the wait and the read
      now share one deadline, and a wait that consumed the budget settles
      [] without evaluating.
    - tab.goto passed any string to page.goto, so a file:// URL would have
      handed local file contents to the tab's evaluate and snapshot reads;
      goto is gated to http(s) before the navigation runs.
    - Synthesized CDP error responses carried no code, so a reply orphaned
      by a target crash tripped Playwright's internal assert and tore down
      the whole transport; they now carry -32001, the orphan-swallow code.
    - A dialog already open when a tab attaches is replayed by neither
      Chrome nor Playwright, so the DIALOG_OPEN gate stayed blind while the
      modal blocked the renderer; registration now probes the renderer and
      gates the tab on an unanswered probe, with getJsDialog reporting it
      under a stable handle whose accept/dismiss run over CDP.
    - A dialog opening Playwright never delivered stayed in the trace
      forever and swallowed the charge of every later dialog on the tab; a
      closed, undelivered entry is retired once the dispatcher turn has
      passed.
    - snapshotRefLocator validated only the ref's shape, so a ref from a
      pre-navigation snapshot could act on whichever element the new
      document happened to hand the same string; refs are bound to the
      snapshot that emitted them and cleared on main-frame navigation.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

The pinned parent 91a868d9c183e46771993aff89c7f7bbfd509b25 has no packages/browser-use paths, so the scoped Browser Use implementation is absent before the pinned commit.

The pinned commit is titled feat(browser-use): add Playwright-based Browser SDK (#11241), has parent 91a868d9c183e46771993aff89c7f7bbfd509b25, and is not identified by its commit subject as the issue-11609 concurrent-session change.
The pinned commit adds the browser-use design documents and the packages/browser-use implementation and test package; the scoped diff contains 50 added files and 16,598 added lines.

The checked-in Browser Use design states that one Browser Use session may be active for the current OS user, one session may control multiple tabs, a second session fails with BROWSER_USE_BUSY, disconnects invalidate the current Playwright connection, and handles from the disconnected generation are never silently rebound.
The checked-in design explicitly classifies concurrent sessions as future work and says that support must isolate tab ownership, event routing, cleanup, and reconnect behavior.

ChromeExtensionTransport owns one local server socket; when listen fails with an active socket it checks that the path is a live socket and reports BROWSER_USE_BUSY, while start/stop promises and accepted-socket cleanup coordinate overlapping lifecycle operations.
The transport test starts an owner on a socket, connects a validated peer, verifies a contender fails with BROWSER_USE_BUSY, and verifies the original owner continues to serve requests.

BrowserModel serializes register and unregister operations per provider tab, tracks admitted and owned tabs, rejects new work once closing begins, and releases attachments only through the live bridge; attach failures release the tab before propagating the error.

The Playwright transport tests cover a partial attachment drained once on close, tab removal during attach, waiting for a pending release before reattaching the same tab, and refusing to release old attachments through a replacement bridge connection.

PlaywrightSession invalidates all tracked tabs on bridge disconnect, rotates the tab-id generation prefix, clears tab/discovery/selection/browser/context state, and rejects old-generation identifiers as stale rather than rebinding them.

Runtime tests verify that transport disconnect makes public tab handles fail with STALE_BROWSER_SESSION, reconnecting creates a different tab generation, old handles remain stale, concurrent stops join until debugger release completes, and an admitted attachment is drained before stop completes.

The design documents the shutdown ordering: attachment/release are serialized per provider tab, close rejects new attachments and waits for admitted work, runtime stop drains registration and transport cleanup before bridge stop, and reconnect waits for old cleanup so it cannot detach newly claimed tabs.

unresolved_questions: The issue body, comments, timeline, author/review discussion, and linked pull requests are unavailable, so the bundle supplies no independent requirement or resolution link beyond the issue title and pinned ref.

The pinned commit is an implementation-bearing Browser Use SDK change, but its own design and tests enforce one active session per OS user and explicitly defer concurrent-session isolation; it cannot support the requested issue claim without inventing a solution absent from the checkout at the cutoff.
A different implementation boundary or linked resolution commit is required before extracting target Change Actions and an Issue Workflow for concurrent sessions sharing a Chrome profile.
Later or descendant commits and their target tests were not used because the extraction contract forbids allowing a target solution ref or descendant commit to leak into the bounded episode.
